analysis.title: Impartial analysis of Measure DD

text: CITY ATTORNEY IMPARTIAL ANALYSIS OF MEASURE DD

Measure DD asks the voters of the City of San Bruno whether they want to repeal the City of San Bruno Safe and Sane Fireworks Ordinance to prohibit the sale, use, and discharge of safe and sane fireworks in the City of San Bruno.

Measure DD was placed on the ballot by the San Bruno City Council. This measure, if approved by the voters, adopts an ordinance to amend Chapter 6.50 of the San Bruno Municipal Code to prohibit the sale, use, and discharge of safe and sane fireworks in the City of San Bruno.

In 2005, the voters of the City of San Bruno approved an initiative measure adopting an ordinance to add Chapter 6.50 to the San Bruno Municipal Code. Chapter 6.50 permits the limited sale, use, and discharge of "safe and sane fireworks," defined by the California Health and Safety Code to mean "any fireworks that have been approved by the United States Consumer Product Safety Commission and that have been carefully examined and tested by the State Fire Marshal and determined by the State Fire Marshal that the fireworks meet and are in compliance with the general and specific standards for design, construction, performance, and labeling for safe and sane fireworks, as set forth in Chapter 6 (commencing with Section 979) of Division 1 of Title 19 of the California Code of Regulations, as it reads on July 1, 2023."

Measure DD will become effective only if approved by a majority of the voters voting on the measure. A "yes" vote on Measure DD is a vote to prohibit the sale, use and discharge of safe and sane fireworks in the City of San Bruno. A no" vote on Measure DD is a vote to continue the limited sale, use and discharge of safe and sane fireworks in the City of San Bruno, as provided by the current Chapter 6.50 of the San Bruno Municipal Code.
Is/ Trisha Ortiz,
City Attorney for the City of San Bruno

Argument in Favor of Measure In 2005 San Bruno voters approved the sale and use of "Safe and Sane" fireworks. Since then, State Fire Marshal maps have identified much of San Bruno is located within high fire hazard severity zones, requiring additional precautions from property owners and increased inspection responsibilities for the Fire Department. In this environment, even state-approved fireworks present fire risks that cannot be completely eliminated. In recent years, fireworks related incidents have resulted in between 5 and 11 fires annually, including exterior and structural fires. One incident caused an estimated $200,000 in damage to a single home. These events place strain on emergency response resources, increase risk to residents and firefighters, and create preventable hazards during a time of heightened regional wildfire concern. Across the Bay Area, most communities have already moved away from consumer fireworks. San Bruno and Pacifica are now the only cities in San Mateo County that still permit "Safe and Sane" fireworks. Ending their sale and use would align San Bruno with current regional public safety practices. It is important to acknowledge that several local nonprofit organizations have historically relied on fireworks sales as a seasonal fundraising opportunity. Their contributions to the community are valuable, and the loss of this revenue source is a meaningful consideration. However, the measure focuses on balancing that impact with the broader responsibility to reduce fire risk, protect homes, and support the safety of residents and first responders. This measure simply asks voters whether the City should repeal the existing ordinance and prohibit "Safe and Sane" fireworks. It is a practical, safety-focused decision.

text: ARGUMENT AGAINST MEASURE Vote NO to Protect San Bruno's Nonprofits, Community Services, and Public Safety Every Fourth of July, San Bruno's nonprofit organizations raise funds that stay right here in our community. These local volunteers support youth sports, veterans' programs, scholarships, camps, school activities, community projects, and families in need. For many of these organizations, this is their largest fundraiser of the year. For years, these nonprofit organizations have done more than support community programs. They have also helped fund San Bruno's Fourth of July public safety efforts, contributing tens of thousands of dollars annually toward police services, fire prevention, public education, inspections, enforcement, and cleanup activities. Everyone agrees that illegal fireworks are dangerous and should be stopped. But Measure does not stop illegal fireworks. Illegal fireworks are already illegal. Criminals who ignore today's laws will not obey tomorrow's ban. Instead, Measure eliminates one of San Bruno 's most successful nonprofit fundraising programs while the City continues to face the growing challenge of illegal fireworks without the long-standing financial support provided by local nonprofit organizations. For decades, San Bruno nonprofits have partnered with the City to strengthen our community and support Fourth of July public safety efforts. Measure ends that partnership, Measure does not stop illegal fireworks. It eliminates funding for local nonprofits and public safety efforts that will still be needed to protect San Bruno neighborhoods,

Protect our local nonprofits. Protect the community services they provide and their support for San Bruno's public safuy efforts. Focus enforcement where it belongs: on illegal fireworks. Vote NO on Measure Daimhin Kirwan, Commander San Bruno Police Association Robert Luttrell, Vice President Parent Boosters of 72 Jennifer Berliner, Fundraising Director San Bruno Youth Baseball Mike Yip, Fundraising Coordinator/Board Member SanBruno Soccer Stephan Marshall, San Bruno Resident

text: Vote NO on Measure DD — Protect Public Safety and Nonprofit Funding

Supporters of Measure DD cite "fireworks-related" incidents, but they do not tell you how many involved legal, State Fire Marshal-approved Safe and Sane fireworks and how many involved illegal aerial fireworks and explosives. That distinction matters.

Recent City reports show that fireworks-related calls and citations have substantially declined. Police Chief Matt Lethin has stated that the decrease is significant enough that the department expects to use a reduced operational approach in future years.
That progress shows that education, prevention, and enforcement efforts are working.
San Bruno's nonprofit organizations have sold legal fireworks to fund services to our community for decades while also helping fund Fourth of July public safety efforts.
The legal fireworks program helps support police services, fire prevention, public education, inspections, enforcement, and cleanup. Measure DD would eliminate that funding.

It would also eliminate an important source of support for local youth sports, veterans' programs, scholarships, camps, school activities, community projects, and families in need. With no replacement for this funding or these programs.

If Measure DD passes, illegal fireworks will remain illegal and enforcement will still be necessary. But the nonprofit funding that supports community programs and helps offset public safety costs will disappear.
Don't mistake banning something legal for solving the problem of illegal fireworks.

Protect San Bruno's nonprofits and public safety. Focus enforcement where it belongs: on illegal fireworks. Vote NO on Measure DD. End Daimhin Kirwan, Commander San Bruno Police Association Robert Luttrell, Vice President Parent Boosters of 72 Jennifer Berliner, Fundraising Director San Bruno Youth Baseball Mike Yip, Fundraising Coordinator/Board Member SanBruno Soccer Stephan Marshall, San Bruno Resident

text: Rebuttal to Argument Against Measure DD For some San Bruno community organizations, Fourth of July fireworks sales are an important annual fundraiser. These dollars are invested directly into the community through youth sports, scholarships, veterans' programs, school activities, camps, charitable assistance, and other local programs. Eliminating these sales could significantly reduce funding for participating nonprofits, potentially requiring them to scale back programs, increase participation fees, or raise additional funds through other community efforts. Since voters approved Safe and Sane fireworks in 2005, conditions in San Bruno have changed. The city now experiences heightened fire risk in designated hazard areas, and public safety agencies report increased seasonal hazards. Although Safe and Sane fireworks are legal under state law, they are not entirely risk free. Any modification or elimination of the program must be decided by voters through a ballot measure. The community must weigh both the longstanding fundraising benefits to local nonprofits and the evolving fire-safety considerations that have emerged over time. Residents are encouraged to review the available information and determine the approach they believe best serves the community.
